study_identification_part.si_4_title: Delineating the Heterogeneity of Alzheimer ' s Disease and Mild Cognitive Impairment Using Normative Models of Dynamic Brain Functional Networks

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Gaussian process regression normative models for each dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) feature (17 a-FCS and 17 f-FCS).
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: We estimated normative models to predict each dFC feature using sex and age as covariates in Gaussian process regression (17,32) in a large healthy reference cohort from dataset 1.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Normative Modeling for a-FCS and f-FCS

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Dynamic FC features derived from resting-state fMRI, specifically average functional connectivity strength (a-FCS) and fluctuation characteristic of connection strength (f-FCS).
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The features (average functional connectivity strength [a-FCS] and fluctuation characteristic of connection strength [f-FCS]) were derived from a dynamic FC matrix based on the Brainnetome Atlas and the Yeo-17 network template.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Age and sex used as covariates in the normative model.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: We estimated normative models to predict each dFC feature using sex and age as covariates in Gaussian process regression (17,32) in a large healthy reference cohort from dataset 1.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.location: Huo2024.pdf.md: Normative Modeling for a-FCS and f-FCS
